title: Same situation with extra goal (opportunistic filler choice)

source.also: L85-CS Fig. 3 (same run, minor typographic differences)

lines.raw: Several plans to choose from FORCED-MARRIAGE LOVERS-FIGHT JOB-PROBLEM
working on goal -- (DO-THREATEN STEPHANO LIZ "forget it")
>>> LIZ tells NEIL she doesn't love him
working on goal -- (WORRY-ABOUT NEIL) -- using plan BE-CONCERNED
Possible candidates -- MARLENA JULIE DOUG ROMAN DON CHRIS KAYLA
Several plans to choose from SEDUCTION DRUNKEN-SNEAK-IN SYMPATHETIC-UNION JOB-TOGETHER
Several plans to choose from ATTEMPTED-MURDER EXPOSE
working on goal -- (DO-DIVORCE TONY LIZ) -- using plan DIVORCE

outline: LIZ tells NEIL she doesn't love him

behaviours_demonstrated.text: RENEE is chosen as SEDUCER because the seduction then also satisfies the pending goal (together renee neil).
RENEE, used in the seduction, is not offered for KILLER; ALEX is used (no 'Possible candidates' line printed).
behaviours_demonstrated.source: L85-TR p. 10: 'Renee cannot take part in the attempted-murder plot fragment, as she was involved in the earlier seduction.'

behaviours_demonstrated.text: The second seed goal (together renee neil) is never 'worked on' explicitly, it was satisfied by the seduction.

differences_from_fig4: Seed churn arguments reversed: (churn liz neil) here vs (churn neil liz) in Fig. 4; trace bindings are identical, so churn appears symmetric in this fragment's matching.
No '-- using plan SEDUCTION' line before the candidate list.
Fig. 4 prints 'Possible candidates -- RENEE ALEX' for KILLER; Fig. 5 prints none (single candidate after exclusion?).
published_version: Poetics 14 (1985) Table 5, p. 491: the same trace; the BREAK-UP plan name is printed "BREAK UP".
